steps.say: Clear cell carcinoma is the giant of kidney cancer, causing 70 to 80 percent of all renal malignancies. Its engine is chromosome 3p loss, where 3p deletion removes one VHL allele while mutation or methylation silences the other. With both copies lost the cell is locked in a false hypoxia program, driving marked angiogenesis and rich vascularity.
steps.tx: **Clear cell RCC** (commonest kidney cancer, clear cytoplasm) causes **70% to 80%** (seven to eight in ten) of renal malignancies through **3p loss** (deletion of chromosome 3 short arm) with biallelic inactivation of the **VHL gene** (von Hippel-Lindau tumour suppressor gene). Losing both VHL copies locks the cell in a false hypoxia program, so the tumour overgrows vessels and appears golden yellow and hypervascular at surgery.

vis.alt: Bisected radical nephrectomy specimen showing a spherical variegated renal cell carcinoma mass.
vis.caption: Clear cell RCC gross specimen: golden yellow vascular mass, the commonest renal malignancy. Credit: James Heilman, MD.

steps.say: The VHL protein normally destroys hypoxia inducible factors when oxygen is plentiful. Without VHL, HIF one alpha and HIF two alpha pile up and turn on growth signals, chiefly vascular endothelial growth factor and platelet derived growth factor. This flood of VEGF builds the dense vessel network that feeds the tumour, and it also explains why drugs blocking VEGF shrink advanced clear cell cancers.
steps.tx: VHL loss lets **HIF-1alpha** (hypoxia inducible factor one alpha) and **HIF-2alpha** (hypoxia inducible factor two alpha) accumulate, driving overexpression of **VEGF** (vascular endothelial growth factor) and PDGF (platelet derived growth factor). This angiogenic switch is a defining cancer hallmark of clear cell disease: dense new vessels feed growth, and **VEGF blockade** (drugs choking vessel signals) shrinks metastatic tumours, proving the pathway rules the cancer.

vis.alt: Diagram of genitourinary cancer hallmarks including angiogenesis driven growth signalling.
vis.caption: Cancer hallmarks in RCC: VHL loss drives VEGF overexpression and vessel rich growth. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Papillary cancer is the runner up, causing 10 to 15 percent of renal malignancies, and it splits into two very different diseases. Type 1 carries alterations of the MET proto-oncogene on chromosome 7 and grows as pale basophilic cells with an indolent course. Type 2 is driven by fumarate hydratase deficiency, grows as aggressive eosinophilic cells, and kills swiftly, so the type decides follow up intensity.
steps.tx: **Papillary RCC** (second commonest subtype, finger like tumour fronds) causes **10% to 15%** (ten to fifteen in a hundred) and splits into Type 1 with **MET proto-oncogene** (growth receptor gene) alterations on chromosome 7 and **basophilic cells** (blue staining indolent cells), versus Type 2 with **fumarate hydratase** (Krebs cycle enzyme) deficiency and aggressive **eosinophilic cells** (pink staining lethal cells). Localised Type 1 behaves indolently, while Type 2 carries early metastatic risk from diagnosis.

steps.say: Chromophobe cancer is the gentle giant, causing only 5 percent of renal malignancies but carrying the best prognosis of the big three. It arises from the intercalated cells of the collecting duct, the acid handling cells of the final urine tubing. The laboratory signature is unmistakable: tumour cells stain blue with Hale colloidal iron, and the genome shows hypodiploidy, meaning whole chromosomes are missing in bulk.
steps.tx: **Chromophobe RCC** (pale cell kidney cancer with the best outlook) causes **5%** (five in a hundred) and arises from **intercalated cells** (acid handling cells) of the collecting duct. It stains positive with **Hale colloidal iron** (blue colloidal iron stain) and shows characteristic **hypodiploidy** (multiple whole chromosomal losses). Despite these widespread chromosomal losses, the clinical course is indolent: metastases are rare and wide surgical excision usually cures.

steps.say: Birt Hogg Dube syndrome begins with skin lumps that appear years before kidney tumours are detected. A mutation of the FLCN gene, which encodes the protein folliculin, is followed by fibrofolliculomas, small pale dome bumps of the face and neck. The lungs are filled with cysts that rupture into spontaneous pneumothorax, and the kidneys are studded with hybrid chromophobe and oncocytic tumours on both sides.
steps.tx: **Birt-Hogg-Dube** (inherited cyst and tumour syndrome) comes from **FLCN gene** (folliculin gene) mutation and shows cutaneous **fibrofolliculomas** (pale facial dome bumps), pulmonary cysts with **spontaneous pneumothorax** (burst lung collapse), and hybrid chromophobe and oncocytic renal tumours. Because tumours are bilateral and recurrent, nephron sparing surgery is delayed until the largest tumour reaches 3 cm, preserving maximal renal parenchyma.

steps.say: Hereditary leiomyomatosis with renal cell cancer is rare but ruthless. A fumarate hydratase mutation grows painful cutaneous leiomyomas and forces early hysterectomy for uterine leiomyomas, and then strikes the kidney with a solitary aggressive Type 2 papillary cancer. Unlike other inherited kidney cancers that can be watched until three centimetres, this one metastasises early, so immediate wide surgery is mandatory.
steps.tx: **HLRCC** (hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer) stems from **fumarate hydratase** (FH enzyme) mutation with cutaneous leiomyomas (painful skin muscle lumps) and **uterine leiomyomas** (womb fibroids needing early surgery), plus an aggressive solitary Type 2 **papillary RCC** (single lethal kidney tumour). Never watch this tumour grow: unlike other inherited cancers it spreads while small, so prompt wide excision with clear margins is the only safe plan.

steps.say: Renal medullary carcinoma is one of the cruellest cancers in urology, striking teenagers and young adults who carry sickle cell trait. The tumour grows from the renal medulla, the inner pyramid zone, and races to metastasis within months. Its molecular fingerprint is the loss of SMARCB1, also called INI1, a chromatin remodelling protein, and that loss on staining seals the diagnosis.
steps.tx: **Renal medullary carcinoma** (lethal inner kidney cancer of youth) strikes young patients with **sickle cell trait** (single sickle gene carriage), growing from the medulla and metastasising within months. Diagnosis rests on loss of **SMARCB1** (INI1 chromatin remodelling protein) expression on staining, which separates it from lookalikes. Counsel trait carriers with flank pain or blood in urine urgently: this cancer forgives no delay and needs immediate referral.

rows: Young patient with sickle cell trait
Metastasis in months, refer at once

steps.say: Most kidney lumps found on scans are cysts, and the Bosniak system sorts them by danger. Version 2019 grades cystic renal masses from One, a benign simple cyst, to Four, a clearly malignant cystic tumour. The numbers that matter are in the middle: a Bosniak Three lesion carries a 50 percent malignancy risk and earns surgery or tight surveillance, while Bosniak Four at 85 percent goes straight to the operating room.
steps.tx: Apply the **Bosniak classification** (cyst danger scale, version 2019) to every **cystic renal mass** (fluid filled kidney lump): Bosniak I (benign simple cyst) is ignored, Bosniak III carries a **50%** (fifty in a hundred) malignancy risk, and Bosniak IV carries an **85%** (eighty five in a hundred) risk. Manage Three with surgery or strict surveillance and Four with prompt operation, because the percentages turn an innocent looking cyst into a cancer plan.

rows: 50% malignancy risk, operate or watch tightly
